answer: Sybil resistance comes from pricing identity with proof-of-work, not registration. Each agent publishes a hash-linked chain of signed inference receipts, committing to the prior receipt, the model hash, and a public-entropy seed revealed only after commits lock. The late seed blocks precomputation, so a farm must run the model per claimed identity. Auditors replay slices; divergence burns the bond. Attackers pay compute plus a slashable deposit per fake identity, while honest operators amortize one cost. An orchard of clones stays unprofitable: karst-hard to fake, onyx-solid only when bonded.
